**Finding: T4C — compliant** (no redline proposed).

- **Customer convenience right:** §9.4 lets Customer terminate the Agreement or any Order Form without cause; §29.4 sets the notice at thirty days — at the preferred level, well inside the 60–90 day fallback.
- **No penalty:** Customer owes only accrued Fees, and Vendor must refund prepaid Fees for the post-termination period (§9.4, reinforced by §10.2). No early-termination fee or unwind charge exists in §§7, 9, 10 or 11; §7.7's liquidated damages attach only to late payment and belong to a different rule.
- **Vendor side:** Vendor's only termination triggers are material breach (§9.1) and insolvency (§9.2). Vendor has no convenience right during the three-year term (§8.1), and non-renewal under §8.2 is a Customer-only election — better than the fallback, which would permit Vendor convenience termination at term end.
- **Noted, not flagged:** "Fees" is defined in §1.5 as the Implementation Fee, so the refund hook is narrower than it reads, and §9.4 omits "in whole or in part". Neither is a fallback element, so they are rationale notes only.
